item.title: Gromov hyperbolicity and uniformity
item.description: arXiv:2611.05416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we first exhibit an example which answers negatively to a question posed by Herron et al. in 2008. That is, there is a rectifiably connected open set in a proper geodesic metric space so that it is Gromov hyperbolic with respect to the quasihyperbolic metric, and its Gromov boundary endowed with a visual metric is naturally bilipschitz equivalent to its metric boundary, but it is not uniform. Moreover, two positive answers are given under additional hypotheses. It is shown that a metric space is uniform if and only if it is Gromov hyperbolic and the natural map between its Gromov closure and its metric completion exists and satisfies a relatively quasisymmetric condition. Both bounded and unbounded cases are in our considerations via two different uniformization theorems developed recently by Bonk et al. and the first author, respectively. Finally, we characterize uniform metric spaces with uniformly perfect boundaries in terms of Gromov hyperbolicity and Teichm\"uller's displacement property.
item.dc:creator: Qingshan Zhou

item.title: Isosceles sets in Euclidean spaces of dimension nine to twenty-two
item.description: arXiv:2611.05421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erd\H{o}s asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The answer was known for $d\le 8$, the last cases being due to Ionin. We prove that $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\binom{d+1}{2}+1$ for $9\le d\le 21$ and $\mathrm{iso}(22)=276$, and that the extremal set is unique: for $d\le21$ it is the set of midpoints of the edges of a regular simplex together with its centroid, and for $d=22$ it is the McLaughlin configuration together with its centre. For $10\le d\le22$ every isosceles set with more than $\binom d2+3$ points is a two-distance set or a spherical two-distance set together with its centre, and the number $\binom d2+3$ is attained. The proof combines Blokhuis' decomposition of isosceles sets into mutually orthogonal two-distance sets, for which we give a short self-contained proof (the key step is a special case of Gallai's theorem on edge colourings without rainbow triangles), with the recent determination of the maximum two-distance sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $9\le d\le22$ and with the known maximum sizes of spherical two-distance sets. In dimension nine this gives only $\mathrm{iso}(9)\le47$, and the exact value $46$ requires an additional argument about eight-dimensional two-distance sets with at least $44$ points. We also show that $\mathrm{iso}(23)=\max\{g(23),278\}$, where $g(23)$ is the largest size of a two-distance set in $\mathbb{R}^{23}$, so that $278\le\mathrm{iso}(23)\le575$.
item.dc:creator: Hyunjun Yi

item.title: Logarithmically Slim Polygons
item.description: arXiv:2611.05429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the relationship between the large-scale geometry of a geodesic metric space and the slimness of its geodesic polygons. We show that if there is a uniform constant $\delta$ such that every geodesic polygon in an unbounded geodesic metric space is $\delta$-slim, then the space has asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one. We further consider graphs of bounded valency and allow the slimness constant of an $n$-gon to grow logarithmically with $n$. More precisely, under an explicit logarithmic bound on the slimness of geodesic $n$-gons, we prove that the graph has asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one. Thus, sufficiently strong logarithmic control on the slimness of geodesic polygons forces one-dimensional large-scale geometry. We also obtain two criteria for graphs, outside the hyperbolic setting, to have asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one. In particular, these criteria show that one-dimensional large-scale geometry can be detected from quantitative restrictions on the slimness of geodesic polygons, without requiring the space to be hyperbolic.
item.dc:creator: Panagiotis Tselekidis

item.title: Filling Lipschitz spheres in metric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.05513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a homotopical Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Lipschitz maps from the unit n-sphere into metric spaces admitting a bounded bicombing, which includes CAT(0)-spaces and normed vector spaces. To do so, we first refine the second-named author's Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for singular Lipschitz chains to this setting. Then, we show that a singular Lipschitz chain filling induces a Lipschitz map filling of almost the same volume or less, by adapting a strategy seen in work of Gromov and others.
item.dc:creator: Noa Vikman, Stefan Wenger

item.title: Scaling Limits and Fractal Dimensions of $\omega$-Substitution Graph Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.05960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a class of non-homogeneous self-similar constructions, called $\omega $-substitution graph system, in which the interface vertices are determined by an infinite sequence $\omega .$ The associated graph sequences naturally form compact metric measure spaces, and under suitable assumptions on $\omega$, we establish their convergence in the Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov sense. We determine the Hausdorff and box-counting dimensions of the limiting space. We further prove that the discrete Hausdorff dimension of the graph sequence coincides with the Hausdorff dimension of its scaling limit. As a direct application of the scaling limit, asymptotic formulas are derived for a class of generalized Wiener indices, which include the classical Wiener index and Kirchhoff index as special cases. Finally, closed-form expressions for these indices are also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng

item.title: Hadamard configurations and sharp cubic-period bounds for stealth in dimensions 10, 11, and 12
item.description: arXiv:2611.06148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct explicit, nonlattice periodic point configurations in dimensions $10$, $11$ and $12$ with stealth center density $1/24$ and unit-density stealth radius $2\cdot24^{-1/n}$. These values exceed those of duals of the current record lattice packings, without claiming to exceed all possible lattices. The construction uses the $24$ sign rows of an order-$12$ Hadamard matrix and their antipodes, projected onto $n$ coordinates. For an arbitrary, not necessarily binary, equally weighted motif with marked period $2\mathbb{Z}^n$, we prove a sharp $2n$-point lower bound for a raw stealth radius at least one and classify equality by antipodal Hadamard configurations. We deduce bounded-complexity optimality, sharp optimality among binary motifs in dimensions $10$--$12$, and local maximality under simultaneous perturbations of the motif and the marked period shape. A divisibility argument excludes ordinary equally weighted periodic formal duals. Statements are confined to their indicated classes; no global optimality among arbitrary-period configurations is asserted.
item.dc:creator: Josiah Park

item.title: Uniqueness of the hexagonal lattice's universal optimality
item.description: arXiv:2611.06278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We build on a recent proof of the universal optimality of the planar hexagonal lattice. We extend this result to demonstrate that, up to Euclidean motion, the hexagonal lattice is the only periodic configuration with this property.
item.dc:creator: Markus Faulhuber, Philipp Petersen

item.title: On the geometry of real polynomials of the 7-th degree with simple complex critical points
item.description: arXiv:2611.06695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider real monic polynomials with simple complex critical points. Critical values of such polynomial $p$ can be considered as vertices of the uniquely defined polygon, symmetric with respect to the $x$-axis. The inverse image of this polygon is a tree-like system of ovals that touch each other externally in critical points. This system of ovals will be called the geometrical code of $p$. Let $a_1+i\cdot b_1,\ldots,a_n+i\cdot b_n$, $a_1<a_2<\ldots<a_n$ and $b_i>0$, $i=1,\ldots,n$, be the set of critical points of our polynomial $p$ in the upper halfplane, and $c_1+i\cdot d_1,\ldots,c_n+i\cdot d_n$ be their images. The order of numbers $c_k$ and the list of signs of numbers $d_k$ will be called the algebraic code of $p$. In our experimental work we study geometrical and algebraic codes of the 7-th degree polynomials and the relations between them.
item.dc:creator: Elizaveta Khokhlova, Yury Kochetkov

item.title: On Diameter Graphs Problems: A proof of Brass's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.05631v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The diameter graph of a finite set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ has vertex set $S$ and two points are adjacent when their distance equals $\operatorname{diam} S$. In this paper we study the following question: given $k$ and $d$, is there a constant $c=c(k,d)$ such that from every finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ one can remove at most $c$ points so that the subgraph of the diameter graph induced by the remaining points is $k$-colorable? Brass conjectured that such a constant exists for $d=3$ and $k=3$. We prove this conjecture by showing that at most one point needs to be removed. We also answer a question of Dol'nikov, showing that for every positive integer $m$, there exist a finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ in which every subset of smaller diameter has less than $(|S|-m)/2$ points.
item.dc:creator: Gyivan Lopez-Campos

item.title: Assouad--Nagata dimension of systolic complexes with almost flat intervals
item.description: arXiv:2611.05763v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of systolic complexes with almost flat intervals. They constitute a subclass of fit systolic complexes and arise naturally in the study of graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation complexes. We prove that their Assouad--Nagata dimension is bounded above by a universal constant. As consequences, we obtain universal bounds on the Assouad--Nagata dimension of tame simply connected graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation complexes and of finitely generated groups defined by graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation presentations. In the appendix, we observe that the proof of finiteness of asymptotic dimension for buildings due to Dymara and Schick also yields finiteness of their asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension.
item.dc:creator: Mart\'in Blufstein, Victor Chepoi, Huaitao Gui, Damian Osajda

item.title: Matching Random Point Sets with Minimum Distortion
item.description: arXiv:2611.06845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How well can two independent random samples from a metric measure space be matched while preserving pairwise distances? Concretely, given two independent copies, each of $n$ points sampled from the space, what is their typical metric distortion as finite $n$-point metric spaces? We prove that the space $[0,1]$ equipped with the uniform measure already exhibits a rich behavior. We show that with high probability the distortion of the two independent samples is $n^{2/3}$ up to polylogarithmic factors. The lower bound reflects two competing obstructions. A bijection that maps points close to their original positions or their reflections in $[0,1]$ must expand the smallest gaps, in both directions. On the other hand, we show that large displacement from both the identity and reflection itself forces large distortion. Balancing these obstructions yields the lower-bound exponent $2/3$. For the upper bound, we construct a partial matching of the points that maps each gap between consecutive points of length $d\lesssim n^{-4/3}$ to a pair at distance $\widetilde{O}(dn^{1/3})$, with analogous control in the reverse direction. We then use a delicate multiscale oscillation construction to extend this partial matching to a low-distortion bijection.
item.dc:creator: Itai Benjamini, Mark Braverman, Elad Tzalik, Georgii Zakharov

item.title: Towards Hodge-Riemann relations for non-Archimedean analogs of valuations on convex sets
item.description: arXiv:2606.25641v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In [8], a non-Archimedean analogue of the space of translation-invariant even valuations on convex sets was introduced. In [7], motivated by a further analogy with the classical theory, this space was equipped with two multiplicative structures, the product and the convolution. Both structures satisfy Poincare duality and the (non-mixed) hard Lefschetz theorem. In this paper, we formulate a conjecture concerning a more general mixed versions of the hard Lefschetz theorem and the Hodge-Riemann relations. We prove the non-mixed Hodge-Riemann relations in degree 1 for the product and, equivalently, in codegree 1 for the convolution.
item.dc:creator: Semyon Alesker

item.title: The topology of Gromov--Hausdorff space
item.description: arXiv:2609.09639v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the Gromov--Hausdorff space is homeomorphic to the real Hilbert space $\ell^2$. We construct a continuous assignment of full-support probability measures that is equivariant under isometries and finite-dimensional local approximations that control all pairwise distances. These approximations yield the absolute retract property for all metrizable spaces. We also prove that any countable family of continuous maps from compact metrizable spaces can be approximated, with respect to a prescribed open cover, by maps whose images form a discrete family.
item.dc:creator: Yoshito Ishiki

item.title: Every Compact Metric Space Is Isometrically Embeddable into the Gromov-Hausdorff Space
item.description: arXiv:2609.21469v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(\mathcal{M},d_{\mathrm{GH}})$ denote the Gromov-Hausdorff space. We prove that every nonempty compact metric space is isometrically embeddable into $(\mathcal{M},d_{\mathrm{GH}})$, answering a question of Iliadis. The corresponding result was previously known for finite metric spaces and several larger classes. However, the general compact case remained open. More precisely, let $D>0$ and let $K$ be a nonempty compact metric space with diameter at most $D$. On a fixed Cantor space, we associate a metric to each $1$-Lipschitz function from $K$ to $[0,D]$ so that the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between any two resulting spaces is exactly the uniform distance between the corresponding functions. The resulting spaces have diameter at most $76D$. As a consequence, the subspace of $\mathcal{M}$ represented by Cantor spaces is itself isometrically universal for compact metric spaces. We also construct finite approximations of these spaces, obtain an exact formula for the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between the finite models, and derive uniform approximation and covering estimates.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Fukano

item.title: On solid angles and simplex shape measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.05883v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The minimum solid angle of a simplex is shown to be a shape measure in any dimension. While this has been known in dimensions two and three, the higher-dimensional generalization is new. We prove inequalities between the minimum solid angle of a non-degenerate simplex and its fullness. Up to dimension-dependent constants, the fullness is bounded from above by the minimum solid angle, and it is bounded from below by the square of the minimum solid angle. The exponents are optimal for three and higher dimensions. This work therefore generalizes the minimum angle condition. We also review several simplex shape measures and their relationships.
item.dc:creator: Martin W. Licht

item.title: Approximating the Euclidean Ball by Polytopes: Surprising Rates in High Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34651v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide sharp estimates on the number of vertices needed to approximate the Euclidean unit ball $B_d\subset\mathbb R^d$ with relative symmetric-difference volume error at most $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. We show that the minimum vertex budget $N_\varepsilon(d)$ satisfies $$\log N_\varepsilon(d)\asymp d\log\left(1+\frac1{\varepsilon\sqrt d}\right).$$ In particular, $\exp(O(\sqrt d/\varepsilon))$ vertices suffice for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and all sufficiently large $d$. We also prove that achieving a fixed error $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ requires at least $\Omega\bigl((\tfrac{1+\varepsilon}{2\sqrt\varepsilon})^{d-1}\bigr)$ facets, an exponential number in $d$. We extend our vertex approximation result to Gaussian symmetric-difference error, and give a positive answer to the question of De, Nadimpalli, and Servedio about subexponential vertex complexity for approximating Euclidean balls. We also disprove a Macbeath-type extremality principle for unrestricted vertex approximation. Whereas the ball uniformly maximizes the inscribed approximation error among all convex bodies (Macbeath, 1951), we show that approximating the hypercube $[-1,1]^d$ to relative error $\varepsilon$, with $\delta:=1-\varepsilon$, requires $N\ge\frac{\delta}{2}\exp(\Omega(\delta^2d/\log^2(2/\delta)))$ vertices whenever $d\ge16\log(2/\delta)$. Thus, when $d$ is large, the cube is harder to approximate than the ball in this sense. Finally, we determine the sharp dimensional order of the classical Laguerre-Delone triangulation number, showing that $\mathrm{ldel}_{d-1}=\Theta(d^{-1/2})$ as $d\to\infty$. This improves both the upper bound of Ludwig, Sch\"utt, and Werner and the lower bound of B\"or\"oczky by a factor of order $\sqrt d$. By classical asymptotic approximation theorems (Ludwig, 1999), this improvement applies to every convex body in $\mathbb R^d$ with $C^2$ boundary and positive Gaussian curvature.
item.dc:creator: Yegor Gorodzha, Steven Hoehner, Gil Kur
